o1.biggest_strength: A dated plan with an owner on every step, built around proving carry-over: beta testers with 20+ hotkeys, a backup and restore path, staged auto-update, and a dated plan B with ticket thresholds.
o1.biggest_mistake: The X post credits authors only in a follow-up reply rather than in the post itself, and the creator and author target simply repeats last time's author number instead of modelling the effect of early access.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Name the specific starter-set extensions and their authors in the X post and email, so the community credit and the new-user path are concrete on launch day.

o2.biggest_strength: Strong gates (1,000 real setups with zero loss, top 200 extensions tested, claims locked to the build) plus smart touches like giving Product Hunt its own day and putting engineers on support during the freeze.
o2.biggest_mistake: Creators get the build only on 24 Nov and power-user beta starts 23 Nov, leaving little time before the 1 Dec freeze and the 4 Dec gate, and the timeline has no clear owner per step.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Move the creator build and the power-user beta to the week of 16 Nov, add an owner column and a day-4 plan B, and cut the placeholders from the drafts.

reason: Both rank channels by users who stay and take the migration risk seriously. Output 1 gives me a timeline my small team can actually run, with owners, earlier creator access, a fallback plan and drafts with no blanks to fill.
